item.title: Warning: This Pro Triathlon Gear Will Jack You Up
item.description: Super shoes, aggressive bike fits, and even teardrop-shaped TT helmets may make the average age-group triathlete slower, not faster, says a physical therapist and former pro triathlete. Read the full article at Warning: This Pro Triathlon Gear Will Jack You Up on Triathlete.

item.title: Ironman 70.3 Oceanside Will Go On As Planned (For Now)
item.description: Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, where a segment of the 70.3 Oceanside bike course takes place, is currently operating at safety level Bravo+. What does that mean for triathletes racing on March 28? Read the full article at Ironman 70.3 Oceanside Will Go On As Planned (For Now) on Triathlete.

item.title: Iran War Disrupts 2026 Triathlon Calendar
item.description: World Triathlon has announced its WTCS season opener in Abu Dhabi is postponed due to regional unrest, while uncertainty looms over T100 and Ironman races in the Middle East and travel abroad. Read the full article at Iran War Disrupts 2026 Triathlon Calendar on Triathlete.

item.title: We’re Tired of “These Unprecedented Times” for Triathlon, But Here We Are
item.description: While triathlon cancellations and uncertainty due to the Iran war are frustrating, a brief pause can offer a moment of necessary perspective. Read the full article at We’re Tired of “These Unprecedented Times” for Triathlon, But Here We Are on Triathlete.

item.title: Trevor Foley and Kat Matthews Win Ironman New Zealand in Dramatic Pro Series Opener
item.description: In the 2026 Ironman Pro Series opener, Kat Matthews stormed to a course-record win, while the men’s race came down to the wire as Trevor Foley snatched victory in the final third of the marathon. Read the full article at Trevor Foley and Kat Matthews Win Ironman New Zealand in Dramatic Pro Series Opener on Triathlete.

item.title: After Years of Setbacks, Triathlon Returns to New York City in 2026
item.description: A new race organizer is bringing the New York City Triathlon back to the streets of Manhattan - this time, as the Big Apple Triathlon. item.title: Heat Training Makes You Faster, Even if Your Race Isn’t Hot
item.description: Prepping for high temps aside, heat training can trigger the release of extra EPO (yes, that EPO) and boost red blood cells. Read the full article at Heat Training Makes You Faster, Even if Your Race Isn’t Hot on Triathlete.
